How to choose a platform for your website

A platform decision should follow publishing and maintenance needs.

NITESH PATEL · WEB DEVELOPMENT NOTES · 2026

A platform decision should follow publishing and maintenance needs. This guide looks at the decisions that matter before and after the page goes live.

Start with the real need

Start with the people who will edit the site. If a team publishes articles or changes service details often, a content management system may save time. If the site is a focused tool, a custom interface may be more appropriate.

Plan the structure

Ask what features are essential now. Forms, payments, product catalogs and account systems each introduce ongoing work. Avoid selecting a platform only because one feature may be useful someday.

Make practical choices

Think beyond launch. Updates, backups, hosting costs and the skills available to the owner all affect the real cost of a site.

Check the result

Build a short comparison using editing workflow, required integrations, performance needs and maintenance capacity. The simplest solution that handles those needs is usually the strongest starting point.

Apply this to your own site

Start with the page your visitors use most. Review its purpose, the questions it answers and the action it supports. Then make one measurable improvement at a time.
